v: Another excellent Vivek Athreya film — funny without diluting its sensitive core, thoughtful without becoming preachy. A little long and musically underpowered, but still a definite MUST WATCH.
e: Ante Sundaraniki succeeds at a difficult balance: it tackles sensitive social and family issues without turning into a lecture, while still giving Nani, Nazriya and the ensemble enough comedy to remain a mainstream entertainer. The runtime and music could be tighter, but the writing and performances make it a must watch.
body:
Another excellent movie from Vivek Athreya.

When a filmmaker handles a sensitive subject, there is always a very thin line to walk.

Stick too rigidly to the issue and the movie can become preachy and boring.

Add too many commercial elements and the original point gets diluted.

Vivek Athreya and Nani understand that balance very well.

Ante Sundaraniki keeps its core subject alive throughout the film while still finding space for proper entertainment, and it rarely crosses into either extreme.

Nani is completely at home in this world, but the film works because the ensemble around him is equally committed.

Nazriya, Naresh, Rohini, Nadiya, Harshavardhan and the rest of the cast do complete justice to their roles.

The pre-climax and climax are especially effective because all those characters and their conflicting beliefs finally come together in a meaningful way 🙏

If I had one major technical complaint, it would be the music and BGM.

For a film with this much emotional and comic material, the soundtrack should have added far more impact.

And considering how talented Vivek is and how strong this cast is, there is also a lingering feeling that the final result could have been even sharper.

The runtime is definitely debatable; some portions could have been trimmed without losing the heart of the story.

It may not receive the same universal critical love as Mental Madhilo or Brochevarevarura, but for me Ante Sundaraniki is still a MUST WATCH.

v: More FUN and less FRUSTRATION than F2 😄 Logic can stay outside the theatre — Venky Mama’s comedy timing, Varun Tej, Sunil and Vennela Kishore keep the nonsense entertaining almost all the way through.
e: F3 makes no attempt to disguise what it is: an illogical comedy built around back-to-back episodes rather than a story anyone should analyse seriously. That approach works largely because Venkatesh dominates the film with his comic timing, while Varun Tej, Sunil and Vennela Kishore keep the energy high.
body:
Compared with F2, this was more FUN and less FRUSTRATION for me 😄

I am not sure whether the movie itself changed that much or whether I simply entered the theatre better prepared for exactly what Anil Ravipudi was going to serve.

Either way, this time I enjoyed the madness much more.

Once again, it is VENKY MAMA’S SHOW from beginning to end.

Anil Ravipudi knows exactly what an asset Venkatesh’s comedy timing is and uses it to the fullest.

Varun Tej also does a very good job.

In almost any other comedy, this might have been one of his most appreciated performances — but standing next to Venky in this kind of material means getting naturally overshadowed.

After several attempts, Sunil finally gets a proper full-length comedy role that reminds us of his glorious comic phase.

Then in the second half, even he gets partially pushed aside once Vennela Kishore starts doing what Vennela Kishore does 😄

The best way to approach F3 is the same way you approach franchises such as Golmaal or Housefull.

Nobody is entering the theatre for a carefully constructed story.

You are there to laugh at whatever is happening on screen, even when the scene has no logic and only the loosest connection to the actual plot.

Fortunately, Anil fills the film with enough such episodes to keep the audience entertained.

Once the comedy starts working, you barely notice Devi Sri Prasad’s songs, BGM or many of the other technical departments.

F3 is unapologetically silly cinema — and this time, the silliness worked for me.

v: Strictly average — an interesting, relevant idea buried under commercial mix-and-match. Mahesh is the one real saving grace and repeatedly reminds us how much acting talent is being wasted on formula-heavy message films.
e: Sarkaru Vaari Paata starts from a relevant financial theme but loses focus by trying to simultaneously deliver comedy, sentiment, action, hero elevations and message-heavy dialogue. Mahesh Babu carries the film with ease, yet the writing gives him far less than his performance deserves.
body:
Strictly average.

For me, Sarkaru Vaari Paata is almost entirely Mahesh Babu’s one-man show.

He is the main saving grace 🙏

Audience expectations had started changing rapidly around this period.

After films such as RRR and KGF, a mainstream movie either needed to stay strongly committed to its content, fully embrace its genre, or create such cinematic magic that viewers happily stopped caring about logic.

The old-fashioned commercial formula of mixing a little comedy, sentiment, action, message, romance and heroism into the same pot was becoming much harder to sell.

Parasuram actually chooses an interesting and relevant core point.

Unfortunately, he then weakens it by trying to turn the film into every kind of commercial entertainer at once.

Comedy arrives, then sentiment, then action, then hero elevations, then long dialogues — and the original subject keeps getting lost underneath all that packaging.

The dialogues were a major problem for me.

Several felt irrelevant, lengthy or unnecessarily designed to sound powerful rather than naturally emerging from the scene.

Not every hero can deliver page after page of mass dialogue and make the audience forget what was being discussed in the first place 😄

The most frustrating part is that Mahesh repeatedly shows glimpses of how good an actor he can be.

Those moments make me wish directors would stop trapping him inside silly commercial-message templates and give that talent something genuinely challenging to do.

Sarkaru Vaari Paata had a worthwhile issue at its centre.

It just never trusts that issue enough to build the whole film around it.

v: DISASTER!!!! A Chiranjeevi film leaving ZERO impact is almost an achievement by itself. Story, elevations, violence, father-son emotion, music — everything feels like a weaker echo of something we had already seen done better elsewhere.
e: Acharya is one of those rare Chiranjeevi films that left almost no impression on me at all. Every major selling point had recently been delivered with more impact by another film, while the Chiranjeevi–Ram Charan combination feels driven more by commercial appeal than dramatic necessity.
body:
DISASTER!!!!

When was the last time a Chiranjeevi film left absolutely ZERO impact on me, irrespective of whether it eventually became a hit or flop?

For years my answer was Shankar Dada Zindabad.

Acharya has now taken that position 🙏

The biggest problem is that almost every supposed strength of the film reminded me of something very recent that had already done the same thing with far greater impact.

The story itself did not land because Akhanda had explored similar mass-spiritual territory with much more power.

The violent climax did not shock because Akhanda had already gone further.

The elevation shots did not create a high because audiences were still living in a KGF elevation hangover.

The multistarrer angle did not create an awe factor because RRR had just shown what a major two-star combination could feel like.

Even the father-son attraction of Chiranjeevi and Ram Charan did not generate the emotional novelty it should have; films such as Manam had already shown how powerfully real family relationships can be used on screen.

So the final feeling is simple: there is nothing genuinely new here, and what is being offered is not impactful enough on its own.

The music disappointed me as well.

Lahe Lahe works mainly because of its lyrics, while several other songs sound like they travelled forward from the late ’90s or early 2000s.

And the BGM was so ineffective that I occasionally felt the scenes might have had more impact without it 🤦‍♂️

Ram Charan’s Siddha also feels included more for commercial value than because the story absolutely requires a star of that scale.

I walked out with only one hope:

BOSS, please come back soon.
